title: Unary logspace yields implicit logspace computation
statement: Let $g:\mathbb{N}\to\{0,1\}^*$ have both its bit-membership language and its output-length language decidable in logarithmic space. Suppose there are natural numbers $C,c$ such that $|g(n)|\leq C(n+1)^c$ for every $n$. Extend $g$ to bit strings by returning $g(n)$ on the unary string $1^n$ and the empty string on every other input; this extension is implicitly logspace computable, meaning its output length has a polynomial bound and its bit-membership and length-index languages are decidable in logarithmic space.
hypotheses_covered: Function $g$ from naturals to finite bit strings
